title: Risk-model calibration
text:
This site documents a personal research project. Nothing here is investment advice or a recommendation to buy or sell any security. The portfolio shown is a model portfolio; no real money is invested. Backtested and projected figures are hypothetical and do not predict future results.
This program asked whether the risk model’s weekly predictive distribution is calibrated, and what to change where it is not. The standing battery found exceptions clustering under every single-regime estimator; Student-t innovations removed the clustering on the sealed holdout, and the V3 vol-state dial was adopted for the level bias after every attempt to fix that bias at its source had failed. The window study then made the shipped predictive covariance the estimator the program had validated. The page closes with the full-model assessment, which changed nothing, raised no alarm and had no clean post-freeze week to score.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: The distribution-calibration battery (standing harness and change protocol)
text:
The distribution-calibration battery (standing harness and change protocol)
Logged 2026-07-20.
The estimator-agnostic whitening and PIT battery that became the standard acceptance test for any covariance or predictive change: Cholesky whitening on the model’s own covariance, a dimension-free PIT ruler, coverage and independence tests, and negative controls that must pass before any real result is read.

What it is
A self-contained, estimator-agnostic battery that answers one question: given a sequence of realized return vectors and a model’s predicted covariance for each week, are the realized returns statistically consistent with being one-step-ahead draws from the model’s predictive with zero mean?
The whole test lives on a dimension-free ruler, so it needs no shared factor basis and tolerates a universe whose active count changes as assets enter and leave:

Whiten each week’s return by the model’s own covariance, by Cholesky forward-solve, never an eigen inverse square root.
Mahalanobis distance of the whitened vector, chi-squared under a Gaussian null.
PIT of that distance, uniform under the null and a scalar regardless of dimension, so the Kolmogorov-Smirnov, Berkowitz, and Christoffersen tests run on it directly.
Bias ratio, the root-mean of the distance per dimension, one under the null: above one is under-reserved, below one over-reserved.

Mean-zero track. Nothing here estimates a mean. Any mean fitted to realized returns would compress the residual and flatter a broken covariance, so the battery refuses to touch it. It is a covariance and predictive-distribution test, full stop.
Standard definitions, reimplemented from the textbook. A second-moment readout; Kolmogorov-Smirnov on the distance PIT and on pooled whitened components; the Berkowitz likelihood ratio against an autoregressive alternative; Kupiec unconditional coverage plus Christoffersen independence and conditional coverage on the exceedance sequence. A positive-definiteness floor fires only when a covariance is singular, and is counted and flagged.
Negative controls first. The battery simulates a known-good case (draw from the true covariance, whiten by it) that it must pass, plus a mis-specified case and a volatility-clustering case that it must reject, proving the tests have power. A failed control is an integration bug, not a model finding.


The change protocol it anchors
The battery is the standard acceptance test for any covariance or predictive change. The rules that travel with it:

Whiten on the model’s own covariance in asset space, the object the optimizer inverts.
For Student-t, copula, or mixture predictives use the empirical PIT (a fixed number of causal draws from the model’s own predictive each week, validated by a mixture control), never the chi-squared PIT, which would wrongly reject a correct fat-tailed model. The empirical PIT lives in the regime battery module.
Rank ladders by statistic, not p-value: under residual dependence the nominal p-values are anti-conservative and saturate.
Controls first; stop on failure.
Five pre-registered steps for any model change: a contiguous three-way temporal split with a structurally sealed holdout whose loader cannot run before the freeze record exists; pre-registration of the full variant list before any out-of-sample evaluation, immutable afterward; a trial budget with every evaluation logged, Bonferroni correction on the winner, and paired stationary-bootstrap intervals at the corrected quantile; a negative control that runs the identical selection on a serial-dependence-destroyed panel; and selection on worst-sub-window stability rather than the peak point estimate.
A winner must improve both the clustering metric and the level metric, survive all five steps, and hold on the holdout. A clean negative that survives the protocol is a valid, publishable outcome; do not manufacture a winner.



Where it led
The battery was first run on the live pipeline machinery for the six single-regime estimators (weekly calibration battery), then carried, verbatim, through every study of the risk-model calibration program, the scenario program, and the full-model assessment. It is the ruler every verdict in this log’s risk-model and scenario-layer categories was measured with.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Weekly calibration battery for six single-regime estimators (all six reject independence; the first reading was superseded)
text:
Weekly calibration battery for six single-regime estimators (all six reject independence; the first reading was superseded)
Logged 2026-07-20.
The first walk-forward whitening and PIT battery on the live data machinery: every single-regime covariance estimator rejected exceedance independence. It was first read as fresh-angle evidence for the regime switch; that attribution did not survive the follow-up studies, and the record marks it superseded.

Question
How well is each covariance estimator’s predicted covariance calibrated one week ahead on real weekly data, isolated from expected returns, on the dimension-free PIT ruler of the calibration battery? Because the test lives in asset space there is no forced common factor basis, so a rotating active universe is handled exactly.


Design
Single-regime by design. The six estimators were applied without regime conditioning: one trailing-window covariance per week, mixed regimes. The script’s original reading, recorded before the follow-ups: a constant or trailing-window covariance cannot track the volatility clustering in mixed-regime data, so the Christoffersen independence test was expected to reject for most or all estimators, and that rejection would be direct, from-a-fresh-angle evidence for the regime switch that lives downstream.
The six estimators, verbatim transforms from the regime notebook: the raw trailing sample covariance; shrinkage toward constant correlation; the split clock (slow correlation times a fast volatility clock); the random-matrix eigenvalue-clipped correlation; a library Ledoit-Wolf benchmark; and the hybrid factor model.
Guardrails asserted at run time. Every covariance estimated from a window ending strictly before the scored week; horizon equals step equals one week, non-overlapping; finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite every week, with the idiosyncratic floor firing only on a non-positive-definite matrix and counted; zero mean. The walk-forward defaults to the selection span, ending where the single-use holdout starts.


Outcome
Result: all six single-regime estimators reject exceedance independence. Exceptions cluster. The split clock was the worst row of all six, with a bias ratio far above one and violations many times expectation, reconfirming its earlier rejection. The library shrinkage benchmark showed the least clustering and was briefly crowned on that basis.


The superseded reading (kept for history, as the record keeps it)
The rejection was real; its attribution was not. The follow-up batteries showed the clustering is not fixed by regime or volatility dynamics of any flavor: exponentially weighted, dynamic-conditional-correlation, and the causal Markov mixture all still reject (regime battery). It is within-regime tail structure, eliminated by Student-t innovations on the slice study’s sealed holdout. The six-of-six rejection stands as evidence that the Gaussian predictive was wrong; its attribution to the missing regime switch did not survive. The shrinkage “least clustering” crown was also superseded: an over-reservation artifact (a low bias ratio means few hits, so little clustering evidence to detect), and calm-window-conditional.


Decision
No component changed. The battery became the standard acceptance test, and this run is the first step of the three-step evidence chain that made Student-t innovations the predictive standard for the whole risk model.


Where it led
The regime battery scored the Markov predictive on the same grid, same whitening, same ruler, against matched continuous-volatility baselines, to test the attribution this run had proposed.






NoteVerdict and decision of record: slice study



The slice study’s own report gives “Winner: NONE” and “Distributional fix works: NO”. The decision of record adopts Student-t innovations from it and rejects the constant level scale (model specification). The specification’s changelog gives the reason: the study returned a “formal NO WINNER under the pre-registered gates (a clean negative, reported as such)”, “but t innovations eliminate clustering on the holdout” and “the constant level scale fails the holdout gate”. A winner had to “improve both the clustering metric and the level metric” (model specification); the top candidate, Student-t innovations with a constant scale, failed on level, so the clustering finding was promoted on its own and the constant scale was rejected.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Slice study: within-regime tails and the level bias under a sealed holdout (NO WINNER; Student-t innovations adopted; constant level scale rejected)
text:
Slice study: within-regime tails and the level bias under a sealed holdout (NO WINNER; Student-t innovations adopted; constant level scale rejected)
Logged 2026-07-21.
The first fully governed study: two axes of variants (within-regime tail structure, factor-architecture level bias) under a pre-registered, budgeted, negative-controlled, sealed-holdout protocol. No variant cleared every gate. Two findings were promoted regardless: Student-t innovations eliminate the exception clustering, and no constant level scale fixes both regimes.

Question
Established, not re-derived: exception clustering persists identically across static, exponentially weighted, dynamic-correlation, and Markov factor dynamics (regime battery), so the residual dependence is not volatility dynamics; and a shared under-reservation bias rides on the hybrid architecture, not on the factor covariance. So: does within-regime tail structure (Axis A) fix the clustering, and does a level fix in the architecture (Axis B) fix the bias? Regime dynamics were out of scope as the primary search.


Pre-registration (the protocol, enforced structurally)

A three-way contiguous temporal split, never shuffled: a training era, an out-of-sample era where all selection happens, and a holdout era sealed until the final step. The holdout loader raises unless the run-phase flag says holdout, and the flag flips only after the freeze record is written; the holdout week count is asserted up front from an index-only peek.
The pre-registration written before any out-of-sample evaluation, with an immutable variant list whose hash a rerun verifies and aborts on mismatch.
A trial budget, every out-of-sample evaluation appended to the trial log, Bonferroni correction on the winner’s tests, and paired stationary-bootstrap intervals at the corrected quantile for the bias and clustering improvements.
A negative control: a seeded whole-week permutation of the panel that destroys serial dependence and preserves cross-sections and marginals exactly, run through the same selection machinery.
Selection on stability: half-year sub-windows; the winner must improve in most of them and is chosen by its worst sub-window.
Freeze, flip the phase flag, open the holdout once, run the battery for the winner and the frozen baseline only. No iteration after seeing it.

Variants. Axis A: Student-t innovations with causally estimated degrees of freedom, a Student-t copula, and a Markov mixture with Student-t; Axis B: an isotropic random-matrix treatment, several idiosyncratic-diagonal alternatives (exponentially weighted, long-window, shrunk), and a causal constant scale from the Wishart-degrees-of-freedom logic; plus combinations. Ground rules: zero mean; full-asset-space whitening on each variant’s own covariance; chi-squared PIT only for Gaussian single-component rows, empirical PIT for Student-t, copula, and mixture rows; strict causality asserted; deterministic seeds; positive-definiteness asserted with flooring flagged.


Outcome
Result: NO WINNER, a clean negative. The top candidate (Student-t innovations with a constant scale) passed the out-of-sample gates, the stability rule, and the null tripwire, but failed the Bonferroni bias band and the holdout level gate. Neither the distributional fix nor the architectural fix “works” under the full gate set, and no winner was manufactured.
Two findings were promoted to the spec regardless, because the record supports them independently of the winner rule:

Student-t innovations eliminate the exception clustering on the sealed holdout. The independence statistic collapsed to non-rejecting and exceptions fell to near expectation where the Gaussian baseline clustered badly. Fat margins matter: the Student-t copula alone barely moved the clustering, and the Gaussian mixture alone was again insufficient. Fat tails, not volatility dynamics, were the missing piece. Adopted as the predictive innovation distribution for the whole risk model, with degrees of freedom fit causally on the expanding pool of whitened residuals.
A constant level scale is rejected in any placement. Calibrated on the turbulent out-of-sample era, the constant scale over-reserved in the calm holdout era while the unscaled baseline sat closer to one. The level bias is regime-dependent with the dangerous ordering: most under-reserved in stress, least in calm. The correctly shaped instrument is state-dependent.



Decision
Student-t innovations became the documented predictive standard: scoring any Student-t or mixture predictive must use the empirical PIT. The constant scale went on the rejected list, do not re-introduce. The next study was written into the record: a state-dependent level correction conditioned on regime probability.
Contamination, disclosed. This study opened the holdout era once. Every later study in the program labels that era semi-clean or contaminated and gives it zero gate weight; the only clean confirmation channel is walk-forward on weeks accruing after each freeze.


Where it led

The conditional level-correction study tested the state-dependent scale with the Markov model as the candidate conditioner.
The tail-risk model test had reached the same “mixture plus within-regime fat tails” conclusion at the monthly horizon; this study reproduced it at weekly frequency under governance and localized the load-bearing part to the fat margins.







NoteVerdict and decision of record: conditional-c study



The conditional-c study’s own report gives “Winner: NONE” and “Conditional-c works: NO”. The decision of record adopts the V3 vol-state dial from it (model specification). The specification gives the reason under “Why V3 stands despite a formal NO WINNER”: V3 “fixed both buckets OOS”, kept clustering solved and passed its negative control, and “missed only the Bonferroni-corrected superiority bound”, which it calls “a power limit, not a sign it doesn’t work”; its reading is “no manufactured winner, but V3 is the settled instrument”. The clean confirmation the study designated, walk-forward scoring of weeks after the freeze, had no accrued weeks when the full-model assessment ran.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Conditional level correction: can the Markov model condition the level scale? (NO WINNER; Markov conditioner rejected; the vol-state dial V3 survives)
text:
Conditional level correction: can the Markov model condition the level scale? (NO WINNER; Markov conditioner rejected; the vol-state dial V3 survives)
Logged 2026-07-21.
A pre-registered test of a state-dependent level scale on the adopted Student-t predictive, with the regime model auditioning as the conditioner. No variant cleared every gate. The Markov-conditioned forms failed their negative control; the causal volatility-state dial fixed both buckets, kept clustering solved, and was frozen as the top candidate.

Question
Established, not re-derived: the production predictive is the hybrid covariance with multivariate Student-t innovations and causal degrees of freedom; clustering is solved by the Student-t innovations and is guarded here, never selected on; the level bias is regime-dependent (under-reserved in stress, over-reserved in calm) and a constant scale is rejected. Hypothesis: the level correction must be state-dependent, because under-reservation concentrates in stress. Two questions: does a conditional level scale fix the regime-dependent bias, and does that give the Markov model a justified production role as the level conditioner?


Pre-registration (frozen before any out-of-sample evaluation)
Contamination disclosure, verbatim in the prereg. The conditional-scale hypothesis was formed by inspecting holdout-era summary statistics from the slice study. No parameters were fitted to that era, but it cannot serve as clean confirmation for this hypothesis. Therefore the functional forms were frozen before any fitting, the terminal window is labeled semi-clean in every table, and the designated clean confirmation is walk-forward evaluation on weeks accruing after the freeze, with a re-evaluation script that refuses to refit.
Split. Training era; an out-of-sample selection era that spans both a calm year and the stress years; a semi-clean terminal era opened once post-freeze behind a phase guard.
Variants. The baseline (which must reproduce the slice study’s Student-t arrays bit-for-bit, asserted); two Markov forms conditioning the scale on the filtered or predicted regime probability; V3, a volatility-state dial, the exponential of an intercept plus a slope times a causal thirteen-week realized-volatility z-score of the market factor, with the two coefficients fit by causal regression on training weeks only; and an idiosyncratic-diagonal channel. Buckets defined by causal predicted stress probability.

Correction (2026-11-17). The record has the dial’s two coefficients fit by causal expanding regression over the earlier weeks, not on training weeks only; the frozen coefficients are the last such fit (conditional-scale study pre-registration; confirmation run).

Gates. A raw-band non-rejection gate on both buckets; a corrected improvement gate on the worst-bucket statistic; a clustering guard (a level fix must not unsolve the tails); a shape gate; and a negative control in which the conditioning series is block-scrambled through the same machinery and real conditioning must beat scrambled by a margin (a scrambled conditioner collapses to a near-constant scale, so the tripwire separates true state dependence from the already-rejected constant effect). Stability on half-year worst-bucket statistics, most consistent wins. A trial budget with every scored configuration logged.


Outcome
Result: NO WINNER, a clean negative. Conditional scale under the full gate set: no. Markov earns the conditioner job: no.

The Markov-conditioned forms fixed the stress bucket but over-corrected the calm bucket, failed the corrected improvement gate, and, decisively, failed the negative control: a block-scrambled regime series beat the real one. Crisis-scale magnitudes learned from one crisis did not transfer to the next.
The idiosyncratic-diagonal channel worsened both buckets: the wrong channel entirely.
V3 fixed both out-of-sample buckets, kept clustering solved, passed its negative control (real conditioning beat scrambled), landed inside the non-rejection band, and held on the semi-clean era. It missed only the Bonferroni-corrected superiority bound on a short out-of-sample sample, a power limit rather than a sign it does not work. Labeled the top candidate, non-winning, and frozen with its coefficients and degrees of freedom in the study artifact.
The clustering guardrail held for every variant not vetoed.


Correction (2026-11-17). The first bullet has the buckets the wrong way round: out of sample the Markov-conditioned forms brought the calm bucket inside its band (bias 0.95 and 1.00) and over-corrected the stress bucket (0.78 and 0.70, with bands that exclude 1) (conditional-scale study report).



Decision
Nothing was adopted by this study. V3 was designated for clean confirmation on post-freeze weeks via the walk-forward script, and the Markov model’s audition as the level conditioner was recorded as failed, the second of five.


Where it led

Three further studies tried to fix the level bias at its source so that the V3 “patch” could be deleted, and each failed, leaving V3 as the efficient reader of the mechanism they uncovered: the architecture study, the window-lag study, and the daily realized-variance study.
The final confirmation measured the cost of leaving the dial unwired, and the window study wired it into the production predictive covariance, with the coefficients read frozen from this study’s artifact at runtime and never hard-coded. The standing watch item is the dial’s calm-bucket bias on accruing clean weeks; the pre-agreed response is a one-parameter recalibration under a new small prereg, not a new hypothesis.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Architecture study: is the level bias Marchenko-Pastur truncation loss? (HYPOTHESIS WRONG)
text:
Architecture study: is the level bias Marchenko-Pastur truncation loss? (HYPOTHESIS WRONG)
Logged 2026-07-21.
A pre-registered disconfirmation test of whether the systematic level bias lives in the factor architecture, specifically the random-matrix truncation of the residual correlation, so that fixing it at the source would make the V3 dial deletable. The trace-level version was already wrong at the source, and the surviving off-diagonal version failed every gate.

Correction (2026-11-17). “Failed every gate” is not accurate: the isotropic add-back failed the band gate and the negative control, and the raw-bulk variant failed the band, improvement and shape gates (architecture study report); neither was eligible.


Question
Does the systematic level bias live in the factor architecture, specifically the Marchenko-Pastur truncation of the residual correlation, and does fixing it at the source remove the need for any conditional level multiplier, the V3 dial from the conditional level-correction study?


Pre-registration (frozen before any out-of-sample touch)
Central hypothesis, registered verbatim and falsifiable. The random-matrix cutoff discards eigenvalue mass from the residual correlation estimate; that mass is variance the model never reserves for, and it is larger in high-volatility windows. Predictions: restoring the truncated mass moves the bias ratio toward one in both regime buckets (P1); the volatility-conditional signature shrinks, the calm/stress gap narrows, and a V3-style refit on top of the fix yields a slope near zero, nothing left to patch (P2); clustering stays solved, or the variant is disqualified (P3). If P1 and P2 fail, the architecture story is wrong and the honest fallback is V3 as a patch pending its walk-forward.
Step 0 discovery, verified numerically before anything ran. Production builds the idiosyncratic diagonal as the residual variance minus the diagonal of the retained signal part, clipped. So the eigenvalue mass below the cutoff is not discarded at the trace level: its per-asset diagonal is folded into the idiosyncratic block. What production discards is only the off-diagonal structure of the truncated subspace. Consequences frozen before scoring: the diagonal add-back is analytically identical to production and can only serve as a wiring check; the trace-level reading of the hypothesis is already disconfirmed at the source; the study proceeds as the pre-registered disconfirmation, testing the surviving off-diagonal version (isotropic clipping to the bulk mean, or keeping the raw bulk).
Protocol. Training era; out-of-sample selection era with both volatility states asserted present; the terminal era demoted as contaminated twice (the slice holdout and the conditional-scale semi-clean read), reported for continuity with no gate weight and kept sealed behind the run-phase guard regardless. Variants: the baseline (must reproduce the frozen arrays bit-for-bit), the isotropic add-back, the diagonal add-back (null), the raw bulk, the V3 patch benchmark reloaded frozen and never rescored, and a probe that refits a V3-style dial on top of the add-back. Gates as in the program, plus a negative control that block-scrambles the bulk mass series (right amounts, wrong times). A trial budget with every configuration logged.


Outcome
Result: HYPOTHESIS WRONG. Eligible after gates: none. Winner: none. No add-back beats the V3 patch.

Step 0 proved per-asset variance is preserved exactly; the “discarded mass” claim was disconfirmed at the source. The truncated mass is diagonalized, not deleted.
The surviving off-diagonal leak is small and, decisively, anti-correlated with volatility: the conditionality runs the wrong way, so restoring it cannot move a volatility-conditional bias.
The isotropic add-back improved the out-of-sample point estimate but failed the band gate and was flagged by the negative control: its improvement is a level shift in disguise, with the conditional signature caused by something else. The raw-bulk variant failed the shape gate. Conditioning was not improved.
The P2 probe. The refit dial slope on the add-back’s history stayed significantly positive, essentially unchanged from the baseline. The dial still has its full job to do on top of the architectural fix.
The clustering guardrail held for every scored variant.



Decision
Nothing changed. The Marchenko-Pastur truncation went on the rejected list as the level-bias cause, and the record now states the architecture fact plainly: truncated mass is diagonalized into the idiosyncratic block by construction.


Where it led
The level bias had to have another mechanism. The window-lag study named it: estimation-window lag in the factor block.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Window-lag study: is the level bias estimation-window lag, and can reweighting fix it at the source? (NOT CONFIRMED: the lag is real, the fix is not)
text:
Window-lag study: is the level bias estimation-window lag, and can reweighting fix it at the source? (NOT CONFIRMED: the lag is real, the fix is not)
Logged 2026-07-21.
A pre-registered test of whether the volatility-conditional level bias is the equal-weight window mechanically under-estimating current variance whenever volatility sits above its trailing mean, and whether a properly damped weighting removes it. The lag is real and quantified; no weighting speed removes it without re-breaking clustering. V3 is the efficient use of the lag signal.

Question
Is the volatility-conditional level bias caused by estimation-window lag in the factor block, the equal-weight window estimating average variance over several years and therefore under-estimating current variance whenever volatility sits above its trailing mean, and does a properly damped exponentially weighted or volatility-targeted factor-block weighting remove it at the source, making the V3 dial deletable?


Pre-registration (frozen before any out-of-sample touch)
Central hypothesis, registered verbatim. The equal-weight trailing window estimates average variance; when current volatility exceeds its trailing mean, the definition of stress, the factor-block estimate is mechanically too small in proportion to the volatility z-score. This is why V3’s conditioning variable works: it is the analytic antidote to window lag. Predictions: volatility-responsive factor-block weighting moves both buckets toward one, including the stress bucket every prior fix missed (P1); a V3-style refit on top of the winner yields a slope near zero, the dial deletable (P2); clustering stays solved, with the causal degrees of freedom refit per variant because faster windows change residual kurtosis (P3); the improvement operates through timing, so a timing-scrambled weighting must lose it (P4).
Prior art, registered. The split clock already tried fast volatility tracking and failed badly: over-reaction and noise dominated, not lag. The slice study tested exponential weighting only on the idiosyncratic diagonal, never the factor block. So the open question was whether a properly damped weighting beats both the equal-weight lag and the split clock’s noise; the speed grid brackets that damping range deliberately, and selection is on stability (most consistent worst-bucket statistic, not the best point) to avoid re-committing the split clock’s error.
Consistency rule, registered. The idiosyncratic diagonal is always rebuilt by the production rule using the same weighting as the variant’s factor block; every downstream object responds through the existing construction. No variant may hand-tune the diagonal.
Protocol. Training era; out-of-sample era with both buckets asserted present; the terminal era contaminated three times over, zero gate weight, loader sealed until the freeze record exists. Variants: the baseline, two damped exponentially weighted speeds, a faster speed, a volatility-targeted factor-block diagonal, a configuration with a dial refit on the best damped variant, and the V3 comparator reloaded frozen. Gates as in the program plus a timing-scramble negative control and a flooring gate (routine flooring disqualifies). A trial budget with every configuration logged.


Outcome
Result: NOT CONFIRMED, the middle case. The lag is real; the fix is not.

Step 0 quantified the lag before scoring. The log gap between short-horizon realized factor variance and the equal-weight window variance correlates strongly with the volatility z-score and positively with realized exceedances, and the trouble flag did not fire: the shortfall tracks realized exceedances as predicted.
No reweighting speed survives. The tail-safe damped speeds improve the point estimate but fail the band gate and leave the refit slope significantly positive; the faster speed re-breaks clustering, the split clock’s failure mode again; the volatility target fails the band and improvement gates. All timing-scramble controls were clean, so the improvements that exist do operate through timing; they are simply too small at tail-safe speeds.
The refit slope declines only monotonically with window speed and never reaches zero at any speed that keeps the tails solved. There is no interior optimum at weekly sampling.
No exponentially weighted variant approaches the V3 comparator.



Decision
Nothing changed. Weekly-window reweighting went on the rejected list for the level bias. The reading that entered the record: V3 is the efficient use of the lag signal, not a patch to be deleted; only the z-scored state of the lag is exploitable, because the noise floor makes magnitude-chasing counterproductive. The level-bias question was declared closed as a research program, with V3 standing and confirmed only by post-freeze walk-forward.


Where it led
One question remained open by the registered logic: whether the lag-versus-noise deadlock is a sampling limitation that daily data could break. The daily realized-variance study tested it and closed the program.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Daily realized variance as the magnitude sensor: does higher sampling break the deadlock? (DAILY ADDS NOTHING)
text:
Daily realized variance as the magnitude sensor: does higher sampling break the deadlock? (DAILY ADDS NOTHING)
Logged 2026-07-22.
A pre-registered test of whether daily-frequency realized variance, with several times the observations per calendar window, can be simultaneously low-lag and low-noise where weekly reweighting could not. The premise passed (the daily sensor is genuinely more predictive) yet calibration was unchanged: the deadlock is a noise-floor property of magnitude targeting, not a sampling limit. The sixth and last study of the calibration program.

Question
Does daily-frequency realized variance as the magnitude sensor break the lag-versus-noise deadlock that weekly reweighting could not (window-lag study)? More observations per calendar window mean lower estimator noise at the same lag, so the interior optimum that was absent at weekly sampling might exist at daily.


Pre-registration (frozen before any out-of-sample touch)
Central hypothesis, registered verbatim. The weekly deadlock is a sampling limitation, not a fundamental one. Daily realized variance over a short calendar window has several times the observations of the equivalent weekly window, so the sensor can be simultaneously low-lag and low-noise. Predictions: daily-variance targeting of the factor-block variances moves both buckets toward one, including stress, beating the weekly comparators and approaching or beating V3 (P1); a V3-style refit on top yields a slope near zero, the probe no prior study has passed (P2); clustering stays solved (P3); improvements operate through timing (P4); and even if targeting fails, the daily z-score is a better sensor for V3’s own conditioning than the weekly one (P5).
Scope limit, registered verbatim. Daily data serves only as a variance-magnitude sensor. Correlation structure, loadings, the idiosyncratic construction, and the predictive distribution remain estimated from weekly data; daily returns were previously rejected for full-model use (fat tails, noise) and that decision was not reopened.
Data-source note. Daily closes were taken from the same frozen daily-close cache the weekly panel is resampled from, not a fresh download, so adjustment consistency holds by construction and a fresh pull cannot silently revise the frozen weekly history. A Step 0 audit asserted that weekly returns equal compounded daily returns to tolerance and reported the worst deviation. The sensor for a week uses trading days through the prior Friday only, asserted per week.
Protocol. Training era; out-of-sample era with both buckets asserted present; the terminal era contaminated four times over, zero gate weight. Variants: the baseline, the V3 comparator, and the weekly volatility-target variant all reloaded frozen and never rescored; daily-variance targeting at two sensor windows; V3 with the daily sensor replacing the weekly z-score; and the best daily target with a dial refit on top. A registered rule for how each variant’s degrees of freedom are estimated (refit per variant where the targeted variance path changes residual kurtosis; inherited where the scale cancels). Gates as in the program, plus the comparator rules for “beats V3” and “beats the weekly target”. A trial budget with every configuration logged.


Outcome
Result: DAILY ADDS NOTHING. Eligible after gates: none. Winner: none.

The premise passed. The short daily sensor is more predictive of next week’s realized factor variance than the weekly z-score, at a shorter calendar lag.
Calibration was nevertheless unchanged. Neither daily-variance targeting nor the daily-sensor V3 beats the weekly comparators at the corrected bound; the daily-sensor V3 matched the weekly V3 rather than strengthening it, and the daily targets landed on the weekly target. The refit slope on the daily-targeted histories stayed significantly positive.
The closing finding is in the sensor diagnostics. The longer daily window’s innovation autocorrelation is high: the noise and fat-tail offset eats the observation gain. The deadlock is a noise-floor property of magnitude targeting, a property of the objective, not of the sampling.
Timing-scramble controls were clean; the clustering guardrail held.



Decision
Nothing changed. The weekly thirteen-week z-score already extracts the exploitable lag; V3 stands as-is. Daily data is not reopened for full-model use. Volatility-targeting the factor-variance diagonal went on the rejected list at every sensor quality tested. This was the sixth and last study of the risk-model calibration program; the level-bias question is closed, and the record notes that under V3 the residual worst-bucket distance sits at the noise floor, the reason the next marginal study belonged outside the risk model.


Where it led
The program’s evidence was then reconciled against what the engine actually ran, in the final confirmation, which surfaced a window discrepancy the window study resolved.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Final confirmation: four configurations, frozen parameters only (the engine ran an estimator the program never validated)
text:
Final confirmation: four configurations, frozen parameters only (the engine ran an estimator the program never validated)
Logged 2026-07-22.
The closing battery of the risk-model calibration program, with nothing selected or tuned: the engine as shipped, the engine with the V3 dial wired, a bit-for-bit replica of the estimator the six studies validated, and the pre-Student-t baseline. Step zero surfaced that the shipped engine and the studies disagreed on the estimator itself.

What this was
A confirmation battery under the frozen-parameters-only rule that closed the risk-model calibration program. Nothing here is selection: no gates, no tuning, no new parameters. Every number is read frozen from the study artifacts, and the report presents facts for two open spec decisions: whether to wire the V3 dial, and how to align the estimation window. All four pre-registration hashes were verified before scoring, and the battery’s own controls ran first.


Step 0: the window discrepancy, resolved before any scoring
A spot-check of the spec against the code had surfaced a discrepancy, and the run resolved it from code constants, frozen artifact metadata, and git history, printed as a table before anything was scored. The six studies had all validated one estimator: a shorter equal-weight single-regime window for every covariance stage, with the Student-t degrees of freedom fit on the expanding pool of whitened residuals. The engine as merged and frozen before the holdout ran another: a longer window with weighted least squares soft-pooled per regime, a regime-mixture predictive, and degrees of freedom fit on the window’s standardized returns. Two deliberate choices from two evidence bases (the studies’ weekly battery convention versus the monthly robustness finding that had justified the longer window), never reconciled. So the study replica does not collapse into the engine configuration, and all four were scored.


Configurations

The engine as shipped: the regime-conditional hybrid on the longer window with its own degrees of freedom and the conservatism multiplier at its raw setting.
The engine with the V3 dial wired: identical, with the covariance scaled by the frozen dial read from the conditional-scale study’s artifact. The candidate production stack.
The study replica: the exact estimator the six studies validated, reproduced by calling the conditional-scale study’s own cache and scoring functions verbatim with the study’s seeds, then asserted against the frozen arrays. The reconciliation row.
The baseline: the pre-Student-t, pre-dial hybrid reloaded bit-for-bit from the first battery, never rescored.

Eras carried contamination labels in every table: the training era (context), the out-of-sample era (the studies’ selection era), the terminal era (contaminated by four prior inspections, zero decision weight), and the post-freeze era, the only accruing clean evidence, with no weeks yet. One alarm-level guardrail: a clustering rejection reappearing in either dialed configuration in an era where it had been solved.


Outcome

The replica reproduces the program’s documented endline. The study arrays were matched at the reproduction-gate standard, with the causal degrees of freedom and the terminal dial coefficients identical to the frozen values.
Decision comparison (i), the cost of leaving V3 unwired. Wiring the dial moves the engine’s stress-bucket bias from under-reserved toward calibrated in the training and selection eras and over-corrects in the contaminated terminal era. Facts only; the wire-now-or-wait decision was the operator’s.
Decision comparison (ii), does the window discrepancy change calibration? In the selection era the dialed engine and the dialed replica calibrate equivalently; the discrepancy’s calibration effect is bounded by those numbers. Alignment to the validated configuration remained the documented-clean option, and refitting the dial slope was not licensed either way.
Guardrail clean. No clustering rejection reappeared where it had been solved.



Closing statement of record
What the program’s evidence certifies is the study configuration; every gate, control, sealed holdout, and verdict attaches to that estimator, and this run reproduced its arrays. The dialed engine is certified only to the extent the second comparison shows it calibrates equivalently. What the engine ran was a configuration the program never validated. The only accumulating clean evidence is the post-freeze walk-forward, scored read-only.


Where it led
The window study decided the estimator head to head under the program’s protocol, then wired the winner into production behind a reproduction gate.

title: Risk-model calibration
section: Window study: which estimator ships in production? (CERTIFIED CONFIG WINS; the shorter equal-weight single-regime window, wired)
text:
Window study: which estimator ships in production? (CERTIFIED CONFIG WINS; the shorter equal-weight single-regime window, wired)
Logged 2026-07-22.
A pre-registered head-to-head between the engine’s longer, regime-pooled predictive covariance and the shorter equal-weight single-regime estimator the calibration program validated, each with its own fairly fitted dial. The certified configuration won and was wired into production behind a reproduction gate; regime pooling was dropped from the predictive path.

Question
Which estimator configuration ships in production: the engine’s longer, weighted-least-squares, regime-pooled path, or the shorter equal-weight single-regime path the six studies certified? The final confirmation had found the two diverged on three never-reconciled axes: window and weighting (W), regime pooling (R), and the degrees-of-freedom path (F). This study decided the estimator, then wired the winner in the same session.


Pre-registration (frozen before any out-of-sample scoring)
The factorized grid. Six configurations: the certified shorter window bare (identical to the conditional-scale study’s baseline, reloaded); the same plus a dial; the engine’s longer regime-pooled path bare (identical to the confirmation’s shipped configuration, reloaded); the same plus its own dial, the fair comparison rather than a borrowed one; the longer window as equal-weight single-regime bare, which isolates the window axis; and the same plus a dial. Student-t innovations, zero mean, each configuration’s idiosyncratic block by the production rule, empirical PIT, strict causality asserted.
The dial rule, verbatim from the prereg. The dial is the exponential of an intercept plus a slope times the frozen causal weekly volatility z-score, with the two coefficients fit by causal regression on training weeks only, frozen at the training-era end and logged in the freeze record before any out-of-sample scoring. Refitting was licensed only inside this prereg so that each estimator carries its own causally fitted dial; the borrowed dial the confirmation had used is not the fair comparison. Clips fixed.
Split. Training era; the out-of-sample era as the shared exam, faced symmetrically by both families since neither window was selected on it; the terminal era contaminated five times over, zero gate weight; the training walk-forward reported as a second symmetric readout.
Primary statistic and rules. The out-of-sample worst-bucket statistic on the dialed pairs. A longer-window win required a corrected one-sided paired-bootstrap bound above zero, gates held, no intercept dependence, and sub-period consistency. A match is a win for the certified configuration by precedent and simpler machinery. Disqualifying guardrails: clustering, shape, flooring. A separate “constant-scale-in-disguise” tell: a large standing lift with a small slope. Frozen rows reloaded bit-for-bit and reconciled, never rescored.


Outcome
Result: CERTIFIED CONFIG WINS. The certified shorter window with its own dial is not beaten by either longer-window dialed configuration outside the bootstrap band, gates held.

The longer regime-pooled configuration’s nominally lower point statistic is not a win, three ways. The paired bootstrap favors the certified configuration and the corrected bound sits well inside the band, a coin flip. It reaches its near-tie through a near-constant standing lift with a small slope, the constant-scale mechanism the program had already rejected. And the tell is already visible: it over-corrects in the terminal era, the exact failure shape the confirmation’s borrowed dial showed. The longer equal-weight configuration is decisively worse.
Axis attribution. Window: the longer window is worse bare, averaging variance over more years and staler in stress, the opposite of the robustness its choice assumed. Pooling and degrees of freedom: that machinery improves the longer window’s bare calibration and lands essentially on the plain shorter-window bare, so two extra axes merely compensate for the window penalty they were paired with. Per the Markov-verdict logic, machinery that only breaks even is removed. Dial-matching: the fair own-dial reproduces the borrowed dial’s pathology.
Secondary, the original longer-window rationale, does not survive. Reproducing the monthly bias-ratio robustness read, the study family’s pooled bias is insensitive between the two windows, so the argument that chose the longer window does not distinguish it, while the primary weekly tail statistic decisively favors the shorter one. Both rulers point the same way.
The dial’s intercept tell fires for the certified configuration as well, because the shorter-window baseline is genuinely under-reserved and the dial carries a real level correction; the discriminator is a configuration that beats the certified one only via the standing lift, which is exactly the longer-window case.



Decision (Phase 2, executed the same day)
The production predictive covariance became the shorter equal-weight single-regime hybrid scaled by the frozen V3 dial, behind a configuration flag defaulted on only after the reproduction gate passed: the flagged-on engine walked over the full grid had to reproduce the study’s bare arrays, the frozen dial path, and the expanding degrees of freedom at the confirmation run’s standard, and did. Assembly only: the dial coefficients are read frozen from the conditional-scale study’s artifact at runtime, never hard-coded. The regime-mixture predictive was removed from the predictive path and kept only as the tested rollback; at that point the regime code was retained for the scenario generator. This closed the risk-model calibration program with the shipped covariance finally the one the program validated. The Current Model page carries the resulting specification.

Note (2026-11-17). The scenario generator was not the regime code’s only remaining job, and it later left that one (see the generator simplification): the regime model still sets the active universe and produces the displayed portfolio volatility and the factor variance shares behind the 0.35 dRATE cap. See Still in use.



Where it led

The performance profile portrayed the deployed model across eras and found the one thing it cannot absorb.
The scenario-layer audit discovered that the generator still drew from the retired longer-window regime pool, which the rebase corrected.
The Markov machinery’s third failed audition is recorded here (predictive pooling dropped).

section: Full-history performance profile of the deployed risk model (descriptive; the exception it cannot absorb is a crash at arrival speed)
text:
Full-history performance profile of the deployed risk model (descriptive; the exception it cannot absorb is a crash at arrival speed)
Logged 2026-07-22.
A read-only, era-labeled portrait of how the shipped certified predictive behaves across market environments, walked forward weekly over the maximum feasible span through the live engine path. Not validation: most of this history selected the model. It surfaced the crash-arrival blind spot that the scenario and overlay programs then characterized.

What this is, and is not
A descriptive profile of how the shipped risk model, the certified predictive from the window study with the frozen V3 dial, behaves across market environments, walked forward weekly over the maximum feasible span through a single causal code path. It is not validation: most of this history was used to select the model, so every era carries its contamination label and no selection conclusion is drawn. Read-only on the engine, no refits, frozen parameters, deterministic seeds.
Wiring proven first. The deployed arrays were reconciled against the final confirmation’s frozen arrays on every overlapping week, at the reproduction-gate tolerance: the bare distances, the dial path, the dialed distances, the volatility z-score, the active counts, and the degrees of freedom at the freeze. The run stops if any deviation exceeds tolerance. The profile therefore describes the exact frozen deployed model, not an approximation of it.


The era map and the honesty block
Four eras: the training era (in-distribution; the estimator family, regime apparatus, hybrid, degrees of freedom, and dial form were all developed with it visible, so calibration there is fit quality, not evidence); the selection era (every model choice, including the window and the dial coefficients, was made with its outcomes in view: the most flattering and least admissible era); the terminal era (contaminated five times over by the program’s terminal-era spot checks, zero decision weight, shown for continuity); and the clean era, weeks strictly after the freeze, the only genuinely out-of-sample evidence. The freeze date coincided with the last available weekly bar, so no clean forward week had accrued at run time; every row is in-or-pre-selection sample. Forward evidence accrues only through the walk-forward script that refuses to refit. A caveat on the record: the 2020 crash weeks sit inside the trailing estimation window for every decision week until early 2023, so the selection-era covariance is estimated on a window that still contains them.


Headline behaviour (descriptive)

Net conservative, not under-reserved. Pooled bias below one and far fewer upper-tail exceptions than expected: with the dial widening the bare covariance most of the time, the model over-reserves on average and rarely breaches its tail line.
Stress close to calibrated; calm over-reserved. The model carries a cushion in quiet weeks and lets it out under stress, the dial’s design intent.
The exception it cannot absorb is a crash at arrival speed. The 2020 episode alone supplies most of the pooled tail misses; nothing in 2011, 2015 to 2016, 2018, or 2022 breaches at that scale once the dial is on. The ten worst weeks by realized shock are dominated by the 2020 crash weeks, with the entry week arriving while the dial was still near its calm level because the z-score was negative at decision time.
No clustering where it was solved. Independence is clean in the selection and terminal eras; the pooled and training-era rejection is the 2020 cluster inside the training era, expected and not an alarm. No positive-definiteness flooring on any week.
Dial behaviour. The dial spends most weeks widening the covariance; its correlation with next-month realized market volatility is positive but modest, a persistence bet on trailing volatility rather than a forecast, and its episode peaks lag the realized shock peaks. The calm-bucket bias is the designated watch item, with the pre-agreed response of a one-parameter recalibration under a small prereg if accrued clean weeks show a material drift below one.



Decision
No engine change; nothing selected. The profile is the dated portrait of the model of record and the source of the crash-arrival motivation for the scenario program.


Where it led

The scenario-layer audit asked whether the tail machinery above the predictive covers the arrival weeks the covariance structurally misses.
The arrival-risk overlay study characterized the position-level answer.

text:
Full-model accuracy assessment: the program’s report card, dated (confirmation and characterization; zero refits; no alarms; no clean weeks yet)
Logged 2026-07-27.
The first joint test of the complete production model: the predictive with the deployed expected returns as its location, the first time they enter the PIT, plus the allocation it produces. Every parameter reloaded frozen, metrics and era treatment pre-registered to prevent metric shopping, no verdicts and no selection. The clean era had zero accrued weeks, reported first; everything else is in-or-pre-selection sample.

What this was
The first joint test of the complete production predictive, Student-t innovations around the deployed sleeve-level-plus-tilt expected return as location, scaled by the dialed certified covariance, together with the allocation it produces. Confirmation and characterization only: every parameter reloaded frozen from the study artifacts, zero refits (a full-sample refit would contaminate all future walk-forward verdicts), era-labeled honesty throughout, engine read-only. The prereg exists to prevent post-hoc metric shopping, not because anything is selected: no verdicts, no selection. The battery’s controls ran first and the reproduction gate was re-run against the frozen conditional-scale and confirmation arrays before anything was scored; a mismatch would have been a wiring-drift alarm.


The eras, reported clean-first
The clean era, weeks strictly after the freeze date (2026-07-17), is the only admissible forward evidence and had zero accrued weeks at run time, reported first. Everything below is in-or-pre-selection sample, and “beats” language was withheld per the prereg. The Home page tracks the live book from that same date.

Correction (2026-11-17). The sentence above, and the last sentence of this entry, described the site in July. The model portfolio (no real capital) is tracked live from the go-live on 2026-11-20 (see Home); the recaps begin at the go-live.



Outcome (facts, era-labeled; the pre-registered alarms did not fire)
Part A, the joint weekly predictive. Scoring the with-expected-return predictive against the zero-mean one over the full grid: the pooled bias and worst-bucket statistic moved by a negligible amount and no test flipped between reject and pass. The expected return’s weekly footprint is measured as not material, a strategic expected return making no weekly claim, verified. Joint calibration is therefore the covariance program’s record: selection-era and terminal-era clustering stays solved; the training era rejects as the priced 2020-arrival blind spot.
Part B, expected returns at their own horizons. Pooled sleeve levels calibrate at both horizons with intervals containing zero; the 2021 to 2023 bond rate-shock miss reproduces (the horizon-mismatch exhibit); the deployed ordering’s rank IC sits inside the persistence null band at both horizons, level structure with no incremental ordering information, as the rank-IC and reverse-optimization records predicted, with the minimum detectable effect disclosed first; the known-limitation ledger reproduces at interval grade at the priced signs (equity-core under-credits, dollar and loan over-credits, the managed-futures cell too thin for an update).
Part C, the allocation’s report card. The production weight path reconstructed causally on the re-estimation and drift clocks with per-asset costs. Every expected-return-mode and predictive-mode transition date post-dates the last weekly bar, so the as-run book carries zero in-span transitions and the model of record is walked uniformly. Pooled net return, volatility, weekly CVaR, and worst quarter are reported against four references (a balanced stock-bond fund, equal weight, risk parity, the pre-simplification expected returns), with the finding that the expected-return swap barely moves realized risk, the “label not risk” reading reproduced at the allocation level. CVaR fidelity: breach frequency slightly below nominal; severity elevated pooled and in the training era, with breach depth concentrated exactly at the crash-arrival blind spot, and near one in the selection era, so the rebased layer’s promise held there.
Part D. The closing statement of record, with the current priced-limitations table and the standing watch items, each with a pre-agreed response: the dial’s calm bucket (passive clean-week accrual; drift triggers a one-parameter recalibration under a small prereg); the reverse-optimization equity-epoch caveat (the tilted-versus-flat walk-forward panel); the horizon mismatch (tracked); arrival (the open overlay decision; do nothing stands).


Decision
No engine change. Walk-forward accrual continues on the clean era through the confirmation script that refuses to refit, and a batch review is planned once clean weeks have accrued. The stack described on the Current Model page is the one this assessment scored.


Where it sits in the log
This entry closes the cycle that began with the foundation build. Everything between is the evidence base the assessed model rests on; the quarterly recaps carry the dated commentary on the live book from here on.

This site documents a personal research project. Nothing here is investment advice or a recommendation to buy or sell any security. The portfolio shown is a model portfolio; no real money is invested. Backtested and projected figures are hypothetical and do not predict future results.
This program asked how the engine picks the portfolio it delivers. In July the STARR optimizer and its CVaR frontier were built, leverage was checked and not used, and the capped frontier row nearest a chosen CVaR budget was delivered. On 2026-11-17 the owner replaced that rule with a max-STARR tangency mixed with T-bills, a design decision with no performance claim.

title: Optimizer, frontier and the delivered rule
section: The CVaR efficient frontier, the factor risk cap, and the leverage check (prices the choices; no leverage)
text:
The CVaR efficient frontier, the factor risk cap, and the leverage check (prices the choices; no leverage)
Logged 2026-07-19.
Traces the whole CVaR frontier the STARR tangency point sits on, adds an optional per-factor risk-contribution cap, and checks whether leverage ever pays. The notebook prices the choices rather than picking one. Leverage is not used, but not for the reason expected, and the record says so.

Question
The engine picks one portfolio: the STARR tangency point, reward per unit of CVaR, solved by the Rockafellar-Uryasev representation with Dinkelbach iteration so that each step is a linear program. This notebook traced the whole curve that point sits on, so the risk/return exchange rate is visible rather than implied, added an optional cap on how much of total risk a single factor may contribute, and asked whether leverage would ever pay.


Design (no new modelling)

A CVaR frontier, not a mean-variance frontier. Every point is produced by the same regime-mixture scenario generator and the same CVaR objective the engine uses. A Markowitz curve would describe a different, un-validated model (single-regime, Gaussian, thin-tailed) and would mean optimizing against a model the pipeline rejected. Each frontier point maximizes strategic expected return subject to a CVaR budget, long-only with the per-asset cap; the budget is linear under Rockafellar-Uryasev, so each point is one linear program. The tangency portfolio is one point on this curve. Volatility is reported, never optimized.
Frozen inputs, holdout untouched. Covariance, expected returns, generator, regime model, degrees of freedom, and the cap reused verbatim; estimated as of the pre-holdout recommendation date.
Where the recommendation actually sits. Two exact, additive risk decompositions of the engine’s chosen portfolio: per asset on CVaR, and per factor on variance, the latter documented as a proxy used only for attribution because it decomposes exactly through the factor model at every weight. Latent factors pooled on purpose; negative shares are hedges, not bugs.
The per-factor cap. A constraint on the fraction of total portfolio risk one factor contributes, not on exposure or weight. It is quadratic and indefinite, hence non-convex, so it is solved by sequential linearization with the method disclosed: the achieved share is always recomputed exactly, the requested cap is never printed as attained, and points where the cap could not be met are drawn hollow. The cap’s cost is measured at matched risk. A crisis-pure scenario set supplies each point’s crisis CVaR and crisis multiple.
Leverage reality check. A kinked capital allocation line with a borrowing rate above the lending rate, so there are two tangencies with a fully invested band between them; the borrowing rate is a knob.



Outcome (the notebook does not pick a point; it prices the choices)

Higher return requires higher CVaR. The frontier is monotone by construction and the marginal exchange rate falls moving right: the first units of return are cheap, the last expensive.
The recommendation was a rates bet wearing a diversified portfolio’s clothing. The rates factor dominated the chosen portfolio’s risk share despite many names, visible only because the factor model decomposes risk by source. Counting names is not a diversification measure.
The cap is a diversification constraint, bought not harvested. It costs return at every matched risk budget, so it cannot be return-chasing. Whether the concentration it removes is worth the cost is a risk-preference judgment. The record forbids re-running the sweep and picking the cap with the best return.
Strategic expected returns are not promises. The return axis inherits the un-backtestable consensus level; the risk axis rests on the validated risk model. Trust the risk axis more than the return axis; differences of a few basis points between adjacent points are noise in the expected returns.
Moving up the frontier raises crisis exposure faster than the blended number shows.
Leverage: the expected answer did not survive contact with the numbers, and it is reported as it landed. The notebook was set up to confirm that no frontier point out-earns an assumed retail borrowing rate. A few cap-stacked corner points do clear it in expectation, so the blanket claim is false and is not asserted. The practical conclusion holds for a different and better-supported reason: those points sit far outside the region this portfolio operates in (with crisis CVaR higher still), levering them scales the crisis CVaR that forces liquidation, and borrowing at a contractual, certain rate to harvest an estimated, un-backtestable return is a worse trade than the nominal margin suggests. Return should come from moving up the frontier, not from borrowing. The borrowing-rate sweep reports the crossover above which leverage stops paying anywhere.



Decision
The optimizer stayed as built. The production instance of this machinery is the live allocation: it re-traces the frontier on all history through the latest bar, applies the rates cap, and delivers the frontier point at a chosen monthly CVaR budget (a moderate point, deliberately not the min-risk corner, and a knob), with leverage verified as not applied at each strike rather than assumed. The standing target’s committed forecast is published on the Home page: predicted CVaR at the four-week horizon and annualized volatility. The leverage and sizing layer itself remains designed but not built, which is also why the conservatism multiplier ships at its raw setting.


Where it led

The single-use holdout found the benchmark beat the STARR allocator on return, risk-adjusted return, and drawdown, a real strike against the allocator on that sample.
The mu-sensitivity study took the budgeted frontier point as the production decision object and measured how far plausible expected-return error moves it.
The crash-arrival blind spot is a position-level sizing question; the overlay frontier characterized it with adoption left open.

section: After July: rf in the objective and the delivered rule (2026-11)

After July: rf in the objective and the delivered rule (2026-11)
On 2026-11-16 the risk-free rate (rf), zero in the code until then, entered the STARR objective in the numerator and the denominator. rf is the 4-month Treasury bill from the U.S. Treasury par yield curve.
On 2026-11-17 the numerator moved to the CVaR’s 4-week horizon and the displayed STARR became annualized with sqrt(13), labeled excess over T-bills; the weights did not change.
The delivered rule, adopted 2026-11-17, is the max-STARR tangency over the engine’s universe minus SHY, BKLN and UUP (per-asset cap 25%, dRATE risk share at most 0.35), mixed with T-bills to a 2.5% total 4-week CVaR95 budget, no borrowing. A stop rule keeps the previous weights if the tangency sits at a frontier end, the dRATE cap cannot be met or the solve fails. The previous rule, the capped frontier row nearest 2.5%, is now the shadow, tracked beside the delivered portfolio in the private records; it is not shown on this site.
The owner chose it on 2026-11-17 after seeing the July-snapshot tables, including the instability result: a 1-point move in one asset’s expected return moves a single tangency weight by up to 25 points. There is no out-of-sample evidence (the single-use holdout is spent) and no performance claim. On the engine’s own July numbers the delivered mix had a lower expected return (6.12% against 6.68%) and a higher CVaR95 (2.50% against 2.28%) than the row it replaced.
Rebalancing follows rule B (prereg amendments 1 and 2): every 4th Friday, if any holding, the T-bill sleeve included, is more than 5 percentage points from its standing target, the whole portfolio goes back to target; otherwise the weights drift. Re-strikes come only on the first such Friday at least 6 calendar months after the last, and the 5-point test then uses the new target. The go-live strike is the one unconditional move; the shadow follows the same rule.
